_purpose: Reviewed corporate actions the panel straddles. truth_check --splits warns about an unacknowledged one and goes quiet once it is recorded here. An entry is a statement that a human looked at it, not that it was fixed.
_why_the_panel_is_not_edited: DATA_FEED.md sec.1: a weekly file is an OBSERVATION -- the closes the council saw that week -- and is never edited. The 2026-08-28 file correctly records APH as it stood on 2026-08-28, before the split. Rewriting it onto the post-split basis would falsify the observation log to flatter a consumer. The panel is right; what is wrong is any consumer that differences across a fetch-anchor boundary without knowing an action sits in between. The correction mechanism does not help either: a correction is a full copy of its base and goes stale the moment the base changes.
_who_is_affected: Any consumer that computes a return across the boundary for these two names. As of 2026-10-05 nothing in this repo does. data/market_state.json derives from sixteen names in `series` and no others (SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM and the twelve sector ETFs), and Arena and the Tracker fetch their own bars (scripts/arena_ingest.py, portfolio/tracker.py) and do not read data/weekly. scan_pipeline/panel_source.py would, when it is switched on. NOT affected: sector-regime-heatmap sector scores, because both names below sit outside the 110-name analysis set and no basket reads them. (Until 2026-10-05 this note named market_state and Arena as affected. Neither reads either name; scripts/audit_series.py's review of who reads `series` is in DATA_FEED.md sec.1b.)

actions.resolution: Panel left as written. Both files are correct observations on their own fetch basis; the discontinuity is real and belongs to the reader, not the file.
actions.note: Found while building the daily feed: the 2026-08-28 weekly file was fetched 2026-08-29 (pre-split) and 2026-09-04 was fetched 2026-09-05 (post-split). The heatmap's extreme-move flag did not catch it because that flag only covers names inside a scored basket.

actions.resolution: Panel left as written, same reasoning as APH.
actions.note: Found by the first run of truth_check --splits, three weeks after it happened and unnoticed until then. This is the case for the detector existing: APH was caught by hand, MNST was not.
